item.title: Tracecat Security Automation Platform and Agent Updates
item.description:
Tracecat Security Automation Platform and Agent Updates

Tracecat is an open source security automation platform designed for teams and AI agents, providing a unified platform with everything AI-native security teams need to build agents and automate cyber defense. The repository is available under the AGPL-3.0 license, excluding code under the packages/tracecat-ee directory and code that gates enterprise features.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Unlimited agents, cases, lookup tables, and workflows
  • Build custom agents with prompts, tools, MCP, subagents, and skills
  • Track, automate, and resolve incidents with agents
  • Execute deterministic logic with resilience and scale on Temporal
  • Store and query structured data
  • Turn prompts into automations from Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and more
  • 100+ pre-built connectors and 50+ hosted MCP servers for security tools
  • Connect custom agents to any MCP server via remote HTTP / OAuth or local npx / uvx commands
  • Sync custom Python scripts from your Git repo into Tracecat
  • Run untrusted code and agents within nsjail sandboxes or pid runtimes
  • SAML / OIDC support and exportable into your SIEM
  • Isolated different teams and dev / prod environments into workspaces
  • RBAC, ABAC, OAuth2.0 scopes for humans and agents
  • Review and approve sensitive tool calls from a unified inbox, Slack, or email
  • Sync workflows, agents, and table schemas to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and others

🚀 Availability

  • Sign up for Tracecat Cloud, or self-host with Docker, AWS Fargate, or Kubernetes
  • Runs fully air-gapped
  • Tracecat Enterprise is available as a managed Cloud with US or EU hosting, or as a self-hosted deployment with dedicated support

🛠️ Technology Stack

  • Backend: Python with FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic, uv
  • Frontend: Next.js with TypeScript, React Query, Shadcn UI
  • Database: PostgreSQL

#Tracecat #SecurityAutomation #AIAgents #CyberSecurity #OpenSource

item.title: Agentic Security adds verification gates and accuracy metrics to autonomous scanning
item.description:
Agentic Security adds verification gates and accuracy metrics to autonomous scanning

Clear Capabilities has updated its Agentic Security platform, an autonomous security assurance system, to emphasize deterministic evidence and a rigorous ten-stage lifecycle that prevents incomplete scans from being reported as clean.

🧩 How it works

Agentic Security pairs deterministic analysis with security agents that discover, challenge, and fix vulnerabilities. The platform distinguishes between model reasoning and mechanical evidence. A model proposes findings but never sets severity, confirms an exploit, or marks a fix as verified.

  • Discovery and Challenge: Agents look for weaknesses and then attempt to disprove their own findings through a skeptical falsification pass.
  • Verification: Exploitability is proven where a reproducer exists, and patches are rescanned, linted, and tested before being written.
  • Knowledge Retention: Novel confirmed weaknesses can become reusable rules so they are not rediscovered by a model each time.

The platform treats each finding as a claim to be tested rather than just a list item from a scanner. If a scan does not finish, or if an analyzer is unavailable or a verification step is skipped, the system does not report the code as safe.

⚙️ Key details

The system is built on six principles, each with dedicated documentation:

Principle Description
Evidence before severity Severity, confidence, reachability, and exploit evidence are kept as separate facts.
Deterministic plus agentic Agents are used where reasoning adds value, while mechanical evidence is used wherever possible.
Challenge your own findings A falsification pass tries to disprove each finding to ensure confirmation is skeptical.
Prove, don’t presume Execution-backed proof is available where a reproducer exists.
Learn once Confirmed discoveries are turned into reusable knowledge.
Never fake green A scan that did not finish is never reported as clean.

Capabilities are tracked with exactly one maturity level (GA, Preview, Labs, or Roadmap) in a central registry. A check fails the build if documentation contradicts this registry or presents a Roadmap item as shipped.

📉 Accuracy and Evidence

Independent accuracy has been measured once on code the engine was not built from. The results are low: localized precision is 6/19, recall is 6/278, and the F1 score is 0.040. These quality figures are published with the specific commands that produced them.

The tool treats the repository it scans as hostile, based on a documented agent threat model. To ensure a first run always finds something, the repository includes a small, deliberately vulnerable demo app.

🚀 Availability

Agentic Security is also described as an agentic security harness for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini CLI. It provides a ci entry point designed to be used in pipelines.

#AgenticSecurity #ClearCapabilities #SecurityAutomation #CodeScanning #AIEngineering

item.title: Greenlight Financial’s Luna AI automates 90% of security triage using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description:
Greenlight Financial’s Luna AI automates 90% of security triage using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

Greenlight Financial has updated its Luna AI platform to automatically resolve more than 90 % of up to 4,000 security and risk cases each month, relying on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for the underlying agent infrastructure.

🔍 Overview

  • The Security Operations Center (SOC) receives 3,000–4,000 alerts per month from four primary vectors: dark‑web breach cards, identity and access anomalies, infrastructure alerts, and financial‑risk events.
  • Each alert historically required a human analyst 15–30 minutes to cross‑reference multiple data sources.
  • Luna now handles the bulk of triage without human intervention, reducing the median triage time for routine cases to single‑digit seconds.

🧩 How it works

  • Luna is built as a hierarchical, tiered‑supervisor multi‑agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
  • AgentCore runtime hosts Luna’s agent code; AgentCore memory supports the tiered structure, eliminating the need to build these capabilities in‑house.
  • Tier 1 supervisor runs an advanced language model on Amazon Bedrock within a private VPC, orchestrating more than 30 specialized agents.
  • Incoming cases reach Tier 1 via two paths:
    • Amazon API Gateway exposing the Luna Queue API and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint.
    • Tines SOAR for automated alert ingestion.
  • Tier 1 determines the appropriate specialized agents, synthesizes findings, and issues a verdict.
  • Cases that exceed Tier 1’s confidence threshold are escalated to a Tier 2 supervisor that uses an advanced foundation model with extended reasoning capabilities. Tier 2:
    • Invokes specialized agents through boto3 with expanded context windows.
    • Chains reasoning across 3–5 data sources to establish causality.
    • Produces detailed investigation reports with evidence chains for human review.
  • Different teams can engage Luna through three entry points, ranging from fully automated ingestion to interactive on‑demand investigation.

⚙️ Key details

Alert Vector What the alert signals
Dark web breach cards Card Network and internal threat intel flag Greenlight customer cards found on the dark web
Identity and access anomalies Unusual login patterns, privilege escalations, and policy violations across IdP and internal systems
Infrastructure alerts Signals from EDR, SIEM, Asset Inventory, and other observability tools
Financial risk events Suspicious transaction patterns, compliance triggers, and fraud indicators from card processing systems
  • AgentCore memory enables the tiered multi‑agent system.
  • The runtime operates in private subnets with code deployed via a ZIP file and Amazon S3.
  • Luna triages dark‑web breach‑card alerts, identity anomalies, and financial‑risk events in seconds.

🚀 Impact

  • >90 % of up to 4,000 monthly cases are resolved without human input.
  • Human analysts are freed from the 15‑30 minute per‑case workflow, allowing focus on the remaining ~10 % of cases that require multi‑step reasoning.
  • The architecture mirrors traditional SOC team hierarchies while delivering single‑digit‑second median triage times for routine alerts.

📡 Integration points

  • Amazon API Gateway: exposes Luna Queue API and Model Context Protocol endpoint.
  • Tines SOAR: provides automated alert ingestion.
  • boto3: used by Tier 2 supervisor to call specialized agents with expanded context.

#AIagents #SecurityAutomation #AmazonBedrock

Source: How Greenlight Financial built an autonomous SOC solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
